articles.title: Centre notifies revised disability assessment norms for 8 categories
articles.summary:
The Centre has notified revised guidelines for assessing eight categories of specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, replacing the norms issued in March 2024.
The guidelines, issued by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities on November 18, cover locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment and speech and language disability, specific learning disability, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, mental illness, blood disorder, multiple disorder and chronic neurological disorder.
For locomotor disabilities, assessment of the upper extremities covers the arm and hand, including range of motion, muscle strength, coordinated activities, prehension and sensation.
Conditions covered include amputation, cerebral palsy, leprosy-cured persons, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy and spinal deformities.
Except in cases of amputation, temporary disability certificates will be issued after six months of symptoms. .

articles.title: India, Japan deepen defence & economic ties
articles.summary: New Delhi: India and Japan have agreed to deepen collaboration across defence, economic security, and critical technologies, while unveiling a joint logo to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations, as External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar concluded his three-day official visit to Japan on Friday.According to the Ministry of External Affairs, during the November 18-20 visit, Jaishankar participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue (2+2) alongside Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.According to an official release by the MEA, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific and agreed to expand cooperation in defence exercises, defence manufacturing, maritime security, cybersecurity, and space. Both sides welcomed the signing of a Letter of Intent allowing the Japan Self-Defence Forces to utilise firing ranges in India, agreed to advance project-based economic security cooperation in strategic sectors, and reiterated their resolve to combat terrorism in all its forms. A joint statement was issued following the dialogue.Jaishankar also held the 19th Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue (FMSD) with Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. The MEA stated that both leaders emphasised the growing significance of resilient supply chains and economic security, exploring deeper partnerships in critical and emerging technologies, semiconductors, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, and advanced manufacturing.Reviewing bilateral commercial ties, the two ministers discussed efforts to boost Japanese investment in India and expand collaboration in mobility, infrastructure, and logistics. They also underscored people-to-people ties as a core pillar of the relationship, reaffirming their commitment to implementing the Action Plan for India-Japan Human Resource Exchange alongside discussions on regional Indo-Pacific issues and global developments.Looking ahead to 2027, which marks the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Tokyo, Jaishankar and Motegi reviewed preparations for upcoming commemorative events and jointly unveiled the 75th Anniversary Joint Logo symbolising the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership.During his stay in Tokyo, Jaishankar also met with former Japanese Prime Minister and current Japan-India Association (JIA) Chairman Fumio Kishida, as well as Liberal Democratic Party Vice President Taro Aso. Additionally, he addressed the 3rd Raisina Tokyo conference, highlighting India's economic transformation, expanding global footprint, and new avenues for bilateral collaboration."EAM's visit to Japan reaffirmed the shared resolve of both countries to advance their partnership and contribute jointly to peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond," the MEA said.

articles.title: Anthropic stock makes blockbuster debut
articles.summary: AI Claude maker Anthropic made a splash on Nasdaq on Wednesday as it debuted 34% higher than its IPO price under the symbol ANT at a time when investor concerns over heavy spending and profitability have dragged AI and related stocks lower.Anthropic stock began trading on Nasdaq at $111.50 per share, 34% higher than its IPO price of $83 allotted to early shareholders.The company's market valuation hit $2.09 trillion in the first 10 minutes of trading, surpassing the market cap of recently listed SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk.The stock pared its opening gains, but closed at $97.17, which was 17.07% higher over its IPO price.The company priced its IPO at $83 on Wednesday evening, above the initially indicated range of $70-$78, and expanded the number of shares on offer from 833 million to 980 million, taking the Claude chatbot maker’s valuation to $1.5 trillion despite concerns over the outlook for a key pillar of the AI boom.The IPO price came in significantly higher than expected, despite mounting investor concerns following the dramatic ouster of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, a leading figure in the AI industry, amid a potential Chinese espionage scandal.Separate from the IPO, Anthropic also lined up $26 billion in private placements with major tech partners including Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia.For live updates on US Markets, click here"The ANT IPO saw strong demand, giving a near-term boost to sentiment in the AI ecosystem. Demand for computing power remains strong, so this is not an industry in imminent collapse, but there is a realignment of marginal winners and losers among investors, and those with existing computing power in a stronger position than those without. So hyperscalers, with strong balance sheets and cash flows may be better positioned than those more exposed to the pure growth of data center buildout," said Michael Rosen, CIO, Angeles Investments, according to Reuters.“It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co, according to AP. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.”Strong demand for Anthropic shares, despite a broader tech selloff, highlights investors' continued appetite for pure-play AI companies even as enthusiasm for the sector has cooled in recent weeks."Anthropic maybe one of the few AI stocks that holds up in the near term, while the rest of the AI trade still faces questions," Ben Reitzes, analyst at Melius Research, told Reuters, as he started coverage on the stock with a "buy" rating and a 24-month price target of $155. Melius' target, the highest so far among analysts that have launched coverage, implies an upside of nearly 87% from Anthropic's IPO price.Also Read: Anthropic IPO leaves more than half of institutional investors empty-handedBrokerages expect the company's revenues to around $400 million by 2029. A syndicate of more than 20 banks was involved in the IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley working as the lead underwriters.Anthropic’s stock market debut marks a shift in the AI investment boom, moving investor attention from companies supplying the chips and infrastructure powering advanced models to the AI developers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars being poured into chips and data centres, leading AI labs now face the challenge of scaling revenues fast enough to justify their massive spending commitments.The rapid pace of AI development has also sparked growing debate over safety. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is among those urging leading AI companies to “pace the frontier” and prioritise safeguards. In its IPO filing, Anthropic cautioned that AI could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” without adequate safety measures and regulatory oversight.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains
articles.summary: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday called for building resilient and trusted supply chains between India and the US amid prevailing global uncertainties.This helps countries reduce dependence on one geography, securing supplies of critical goods and strengthening India-US economic and strategic ties, the minister said.Addressing the Indo-US Economic Summit here, he said huge potential exists between the two countries to enhance economic cooperation, as the US offers capital, technology, and innovation, while India offers skills, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness.Goyal said he would conclude with five calls to action, using the acronym TRUST to outline his suggestions."T - the first letter. Let us turn our supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains. 'R', let us raise our talent together with our friendly and partner countries," he said.The minister suggested increasing collaborations between Indian and US universities."I am working with some of them to bring them to India. We'd like to invite all US universities and students to look at India as a part of their program. Because I firmly believe global growth is going to be led from countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. And time spent by students from the developed world in Indian universities and Indian colleges will help them learn how to deal with us," he added.He said 'S' in the TRUST acronym stands for 'Speak', urging both sides to communicate candidly and openly flag any hurdles or difficulties they face."Let us Speak to each other candidly. Let us flag off the hurdles or the difficulties that anybody faces. So that we can work as your partners to help you in your work. We have different arms of the government which will support you in your work. And help you take your work, take your business to the world," Goyal said.He said the final 'T' stood for 'Track', emphasising the need to monitor outcomes, ensure accountability for performance and urging the IACC to hold both sides accountable.He added that India and the US are two vibrant democracies which shape the global narrative and are important engines for global growth."...an engine always runs on fuel, and that fuel, when it comes to India, is trust. India offers a trusted partnership. India offers our trust, a partner who will stand by you through thick and thin. In every crisis, India is that one partner which never lets its friends down," he added.In a volatile and uncertain world, countries face challenges due to the ongoing wars and the West Asia crisis."In these uncertain times, the world no longer needs just supply chains. They need trusted supply chains. In a trust chain, the partner shares your vision, respects the rule of law, honours contracts and therefore India and the US are natural links who build a chain of trust, a trusted chain. These strong bonds are reflected in our engagement at every level," the minister noted.The minister said the country's exports of goods and services have reached an all-time high of USD 90 billion."That is the India growth story. And that is the story we wish to share with our friends like the United States of America," he added.Meanwhile, speaking at the FICCI event, Goyal said that the country would achieve the USD one trillion exports target during the current fiscal.He added that India must move beyond reducing its dependence on the world and instead make the world dependent on India.He urged FICCI to remake itself as a global chamber at its centenary celebrations.The country, Goyal said, now has the capital, talent, entrepreneurs and banking strength to raise its ambition."Last time I came to your AGM, I spoke about reducing dependence on the world and becoming self-reliant. Today I would like to suggest going one step forward," he said, adding, "We need to make the world dependent upon us. We need to create leverage in India".On trade pacts, he said before 2014, India's free trade agreements covered partners representing USD 10 trillion of global GDP, and the agreements concluded in the past four and a half years have added USD 60 trillion.Negotiations with eight or nine further geographies over the next 18 months would add another USD 15 trillion, giving Indian exporters preferential access to USD 85 trillion, or 76 per cent of global GDP, he added.

articles.title: Airtel takes top spot, HDFC loses brand crown
articles.summary: Mumbai: India’s top 100 brands lost 12% of their combined value in the past year, as declines in technology and financial services outweighed gains in automobiles and retail. Airtel displaced HDFC Bank to become the country’s most valuable brand for the first time, according to Kantar’s 2026 BrandZ ranking.The combined value of the top 100 stood at $460.3 billion, equivalent to 11% of India’s GDP. Airtel’s brand value rose 5% to $43.2 billion, while HDFC Bank ranked second at $35.6 billion, followed by Tata Consultancy Services at $24.1 billion.The decline was driven disproportionately by business-to-business and consumer technology brands, as well as some large financial services companies, said Soumya Mohanty, managing director, South Asia at Kantar.Read more: Indian brands hit $523.5 billion valuation as HDFC Bank leads Kantar BrandZ 2025 Ranking“Growth is not guaranteed anymore. The rising tide, which was raising all boats earlier, is no longer happening. We will see strong brands being pulled apart from weaker brands,” Mohanty said.Kantar found that Indian brands which strengthened their Meaningful Difference, a measure of distinctiveness and relevance to consumers, grew by an average of 7%, while those with flat or declining scores lost 13%.The decline contrasts with a 22% rise in global brand value, driven largely by artificial intelligence companies and technology platforms. India has less exposure to these categories, Kantar said.Read more: Adani CFO pushes back on Uday Kotak's comparison of Anthropic with India's top companiesDeepender Rana, Kantar’s executive managing director for South Asia, said India’s expanding economy offered opportunities for mass-market and premium brands, but inflation was weighing on consumer decisions.“Brands need to chart a course that confidently balances short-term pressures with long-term brand building,” Rana said.Airtel’s brand value has risen 210% since 2020, supported by its expansion beyond connectivity into digital services. It is the first telecom operator to top the ranking since its launch in 2014.Meesho was the biggest riser, with brand value climbing 64% to $1.9 billion, followed by Royal Enfield, up 60% to $3.8 billion. Financial services remained the largest category, accounting for 29% of the top 100’s value.Blinkit was the highest-ranked new entrant at No. 27, with a brand value of $4.3 billion. India had three brands in the global top 100: Airtel, HDFC Bank and TCS. Jio was excluded because its valuation was conducted before its stock market listing.

Around 2,000 players representing 123 countries and territories secured places at the competition. All places earned by national teams in 2026 will be protected, with the players who qualified included in the expanded national rosters from which coaches will select their Finals squads.Countries and territories that did not qualify in 2026 will get another opportunity through a fresh set of regional online tournaments, followed by a final LAN qualifier.The regional online qualifiers will begin on February 26, 2027, and run for five weeks across multiple game titles. Seven regional winners and one invited nation from the ENC Solidarity programme will advance to the final LAN qualifier to compete for the remaining places. Game-specific schedules and details of the LAN event will be announced later.“Representing your nation is one of the proudest moments in any athlete’s career. For fans, supporting their country or territory can be their first connection to a sport and the beginning of a lasting passion,” said Ralf Reichert, CEO of the Esports Foundation.“As we build towards the first Esports Nations Cup, we want to help national teams grow together and give fans a team to believe in. Road to ENC creates more opportunities for those teams to compete and for fans to get to know the players, follow emerging rivalries, and become a part of their team’s journey. When those teams arrive at ENC 2027, we want fans to have been part of how they got there.”**Four pillars of the expanded qualification framework**The expanded Road to ENC will operate through four key elements, starting with events organised by National Team Partners (NTPs). These partners will be able to host local activations, friendly matches and multi-nation invitationals, giving national teams more opportunities to compete and coaches a chance to assess emerging players.The events will receive support through the ENC Development Fund, with the objective of building national fan bases and strengthening local esports ecosystems. NTPs can submit proposals for events scheduled in 2027 until the end of December 2026.The second element is the new qualification pathway for countries and territories that missed out on the 2026 qualification season. The regional online tournaments and subsequent LAN qualifier will offer another route into the Finals, with seven regional winners and one nation invited through the ENC Solidarity programme competing for the remaining spots.The third is an expansion of national team rosters. Coaches will be allowed to add eligible players to squads that qualified in 2026, giving them greater flexibility to test combinations in national team matches before finalising their line-ups. Updated expanded rosters must be submitted by January 15, 2027, while Finals squads must be selected by May 31, 2027.For individual or solo game titles, however, the qualifying spot will remain with the player who earned it for their country or territory.The fourth element is the ENC Ranking, which will track the performance of national teams throughout the year. Players will earn points for their countries and territories through results in international club leagues and tournaments, as well as national team competitions.The rankings will evolve as the season progresses, providing fans with an ongoing view of their national team's standing. They will also be used to determine seeding for the ENC group-stage draw and inform direct invitations to future editions of the competition.The Esports Foundation said more details on the ranking system, qualification schedules and National Team Partner-led events would be announced in the coming weeks.The Esports Nations Cup is a global competition bringing together players from different countries and territories across multiple esports titles. Its inaugural Finals are scheduled for November 2027.

articles.summary: The US Federal Reserve is monitoring financial stability risks stemming from aggressive investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and elevated asset valuations, as policymakers warned that disappointing returns from the technology boom could trigger broader financial market disruptions, Reuters reported.Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting, released on Wednesday, showed that officials were concerned about the potential consequences of heavy AI-related borrowing, rising leverage among hedge funds and concentrated exposure to a small number of companies.According to Reuters, Fed policymakers and central bank staff raised these concerns as part of a broader assessment of vulnerabilities in the financial system. The review found that elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were among the most significant sources of risk, although strong balance sheets among banks and households offered some protection against severe financial shocks.Read more: South Korean shares fall over 1% as hawkish Fed remarks weigh on sentimentPolicymakers were particularly concerned about the possibility that returns on AI investments could fall short of investor expectations. The minutes highlighted the rapid growth of AI-related debt, much of which has been channelled through complex and relatively opaque financing structures, Reuters reported.Some officials also flagged the concentration of AI exposure among a limited number of companies, raising concerns that setbacks involving major players could have wider consequences for financial markets and the economy.Hedge funds emerged as another area of concern, with policymakers identifying high leverage and limited capacity among financial dealers to intermediate transactions as potential channels through which market stress could intensify, Reuters reported,Although Fed staff described the financial system as resilient and noted that banks had ample access to liquidity, some policymakers cautioned that vulnerabilities within the banking sector could emerge rapidly despite initially reassuring assessments. Officials also questioned whether existing regulatory data fully captured the extent of financial institutions' exposure to potential risks.Read more: Japan stocks fall as metal shares slide; investors await Anthropic IPO debutFed weighs measures to strengthen financial resilienceThe minutes also revealed discussions among policymakers about measures to improve the financial system's ability to withstand future disruptions.A few officials considered increasing capital requirements for banks, while others emphasised the importance of ensuring that lenders were better prepared to access the Fed's emergency lending discount window during periods of market stress.Some policymakers also discussed the possibility of creating a dedicated asset-purchasing mechanism aimed specifically at addressing financial stability risks.The debate comes as the Federal Reserve reassesses how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Its holdings expanded significantly following large-scale bond-buying programmes introduced during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.According to Reuters, the pandemic-era bond purchases initially designed to stabilise markets eventually evolved into a broader monetary stimulus programme, highlighting the challenges of distinguishing between emergency market support and conventional monetary easing.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has advocated a more clearly defined framework for such interventions, including an exit strategy to unwind bond holdings once financial stability has been restored. She has argued that any asset-purchasing programme should be temporary, with holdings sold in a timely manner after market conditions normalise, Reuters reported.Several policymakers, however, cautioned against relying on monetary policy to address financial market disruptions, suggesting that other tools may be more appropriate for containing emerging vulnerabilities.The minutes also showed that almost all Fed policymakers believed further interest rate increases could be necessary if the economy developed in line with their expectations. Officials had kept interest rates unchanged at the October meeting amid persistent inflation concerns.The growing importance of AI and technology investment in driving economic growth could complicate the Fed's policy decisions if a significant correction in the sector were to threaten broader financial stability.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors PV, other auto stocks soar up to 7%; Nifty Auto index jumps 4%. What’s driving the rally?
articles.summary: Shares of automobile companies, including Tata Motors, Maruti Suzuki and M&M, rallied up to 7% on Thursday, lifting the Nifty Auto index by 4%. The gains came as aluminium, copper and other key metals used in the industry fell to a seven-month low, easing concerns over rising input costs.Maruti Suzuki, India’s largest carmaker, was the biggest gainer in the pack, surging over 6.5% to Rs 13,487 apiece on the BSE, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 4%. M&M advanced 5% to Rs 3,508 per share. Hyundai Motor India shares also rose over 4% to Rs 2,193 apiece, while commercial vehicle maker Ashok Leyland climbed over 2%.Metal prices tumbleOn Wednesday, benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell for a fifth consecutive session, touching its lowest level since April 13, Reuters reported. Prices recovered marginally on Thursday.Also read: Japan stocks fall as metal shares slide; investors await Anthropic IPO debut"The current move in LME copper prices looks more like relief than a decisive turn. The sharp retreat was driven by a buoyant US dollar and growing question marks over the pace of the AI data-center buildout, where copper is a key input in the infrastructure, Reuters cited Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade."The main factors to watch remain the path of the dollar, any further signals on AI-related capital spending, and Chinese demand indicators." Further, aluminum hit a 51-month low, while tin prices plunged to an 8-month low.Domestic brokerage Emkay says the sell-off is primarily driven by a stronger US dollar and weakness in global equity markets, triggering widespread profit booking and long liquidation. Traders also appeared to reduce positions to manage mark-to-market (M2M) losses.Notably, Wednesday recorded the highest single-day trading volume compared with the average daily volumes of the previous month, indicating significant position unwinding and heightened market activity.Meanwhile, China's uneven economic recovery and concerns over demand from its construction and manufacturing sectors are weighing on sentiment, experts say.Higher crude oil prices have also influenced the outlook for industrial metals. Rising energy costs increase expenses across the mining, smelting, refining, and transportation chain. Aluminium and zinc, in particular, are highly sensitive to power costs.While higher costs can sometimes support commodity prices by constraining supply, markets are currently more focused on the risks to economic growth. Rising energy costs can curb business activity, industrial production and consumer spending, ultimately weakening demand for metals used in construction, machinery, infrastructure and automobiles.Read more: Base metals lose momentum amid strong dollar and demand concernsWhy could auto companies benefit?The decline in copper, aluminium and tin prices could provide relief to Indian automakers by lowering raw-material costs. These metals are used in vehicle manufacturing, electrical components, wiring, engines and other auto parts. Cheaper inputs can reduce production expenses and ease pressure on operating margins. Aluminium, copper, rubber, and plastic components account for 40-45% of passenger vehicle raw material costs.Foreign brokerage Jefferies said the earnings outlook for auto OEMs weakened in CY26 primarily due to the intense commodity cost rally. It added that the auto industry faces a high base of volumes starting 2HFY27 as commodity cost pressures continue, albeit at a lower intensity than seen in the first half of the financial year.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. articles.title: Red metal feels the blues! Voltas, Blue Star, other AC stocks jump up to 6% as copper prices hit 7-month lows
articles.summary: Shares of AC majors, including Voltas, Blue Star and PG Electroplast, jumped up to 6% on Thursday as copper prices hit the weakest level in seven months after recording the biggest single-day plunge since US President Donald Trump unveiled global tariffs in April 2025.Voltas shares jumped more than 5% to Rs 1,192.90 apiece on NSE, while Blue Star shares surged over 5% to Rs 1,709.10 apiece on Thursday morning. PG Electroplast, which makes components for air conditioners, saw its shares jump around 6% to trade near Rs 571 apiece.Also read | India’s $25 bn copper drive moves from building smelters to securing minesThe benchmark copper contracts on the London Metal Exchange dropped to their lowest level since April 7 on Wednesday. This came on the back of a stronger dollar, growing concerns over Chinese industrial demand, and the sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks that have overshadowed the tightening of copper supplies.Why are copper prices falling?The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Federal Reserve official hinted towards further interest rate hikes in the near term. Minutes from the FOMC meeting showed that officials of the American central bank saw a growing risk last month that they needed to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they kept rates steady. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Monday said that emerging technologies will have a significant impact on the economy, but the possible scenarios range from rising growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and a potential slowdown if anticipated investment returns prove disappointing. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid on Sunday said that inflation was still "running too hot" and that the American central bank had "some work to do" to bring price pressures under control. Market traders are now seeing a nearly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the US Federal Reserve following its FOMC meeting in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.The FOMC minutes will be closely watched, as they may provide further insights into the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook, which could have a broader impact on the commodities basket, said Axis Securities.Meanwhile, the sharp drop in copper prices also comes amid rising worries over the health of China’s economy, with analysts pointing out that a prolonged property downturn in the country could weigh on copper prices due to the metal’s extensive use in construction, electrical wiring and infrastructure. Additionally, the sharp selloff in the AI-linked stocks also bears an impact on copper prices as the frenzy over the nascent technology fizzles out, raising worries over the spending boom behind new data centres. Copper is essential for electrical infrastructure, making it sensitive to investments linked to artificial intelligence.Also read | Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall StreetHow have AC stocks been performing recently?The consistent drop in copper prices has been boosting AC stocks recently, as the metal is one of the key components of the appliance. Voltas shares have gained 7% in a week and 17% in a month. Blue Star shares have jumped 8% in a week and 9% in a month.PG Electroplast shares have recorded marginal losses over a week but jumped 12% in a month. In the longer term, the three stocks have delivered positive returns in the range of 45-150% in three years.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. articles.title: PM Modi pays tribute to former PM Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former prime minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering the country's first woman prime minister, who was assassinated in 1984.
Gandhi was born on November 19, 1917, in Prayagraj and was assassinated on October 31, 1984, in New Delhi.
"Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary," Modi said in a post on X.
Gandhi served as prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984.
